extractedText: Explore Da Nang: Vietnam’s Central Coast Beach and Mountain Haven Author Thomas Schulz | Passionate traveler and writerLast updated: June 8, 2026 Photo credit: Da Nang’s modern skyline at dusk along the Han River Da Nang is the third corner of Vietnam — the country’s most ambitious mid-size city, sitting at the geographical and cultural midpoint between Hanoi’s Confucian north and Ho Chi Minh City’s commercial south. Once a sleepy port town that served as the main American military base during the Vietnam War (the famous “China Beach“), Da Nang has reinvented itself over the past two decades as Vietnam’s most livable major city: 30 kilometers of broad sandy beaches, a fully modernized international airport, the country’s most architecturally ambitious bridges (the fire-breathing Dragon Bridge, the cable-stayed Tran Thi Ly Bridge), and now the global Instagram phenomenon of Ba Na Hills’ Golden Bridge — the surreal pedestrian span held aloft by two giant stone hands. Add the cultural day-trip pair of UNESCO Hoi An (30 km south) and UNESCO My Son (40 km southwest), the misty Marble Mountains, and a food culture built on the Cham-Vietnamese fusion of central Vietnam, and Da Nang earns its growing reputation as Southeast Asia’s emerging high-quality-of-life destination. Highlights include opening night ‘Nature’ on 30 May and the grand final ‘United Horizons’ on 11 July. Tiered grandstand tickets, with free riverbank viewing also possible. A spectacular sky-lit celebration. [Source]2026-06-28 to 2026-07-04Da Nang Asian Film Festival (DANAFF IV)The 4th edition, themed ‘Bridging Asia to the World’, expects around 900 delegates including 200-plus international guests, with US cinema in focus. It adds Industry Days and five free outdoor film-screening locations across the city and Hoi An. Many outdoor screenings are free. A growing showcase of Asian and world cinema. [Source]2026-05-22Hoi An Memories ShowA large-scale outdoor stage spectacle with around 500 performers staging a 60-minute, five-act show on the history of Hoi An, about 40 minutes from central Da Nang. Performances run nightly at 8pm except Tuesdays, with mini-shows beforehand. Tickets 300,000-1,200,000 VND by seating tier. A breathtaking cultural epic. [Source]2026-05-22Museum of Cham SculptureOpen daily 7am-5pm, this Da Nang museum holds the world’s largest collection of Cham artifacts, including national treasures. A compact, walkable museum, it offers a rare look at the ancient Champa civilisation of Central Vietnam. Admission 60,000 VND for adults, free for children under 16. A cultural highlight in the heart of the city.
